- When sentiment is high (≥ 0.67) and forecast spikes upward, reduce the peak by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is low (≤ 0.33) and forecast is rising, cap the increase at 1–3% above recent mean to avoid overreaction.  
- After a strong upward spike in sentiment, model tends to overcorrect; apply a 1–3 day lag in price correction to align with sentiment decay.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 3σ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast with 3-day moving average.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ 0.33) over 3+ days, forecast should not exceed 10% above recent low; cap at 10% above 14-day low.
